newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares overcome Wall St drop to end higher.
newsitem.headline: German shares overcome Wall St drop to end higher.

text.p: Germany's 30-share IBIS DAX index continued its dollar-driven rally on Wednesday, ending the day strongly ahead, having survived a downward hiccup in the afternoon when Wall Street opened lower.

While dealers are still forecasting a correction, they said they will make the most of the bull-run for as long as it lasts and the IBIS DAX index, which measures electronic trade in German shares, ended at 3,026.63 points, up 25.97 points.
Earlier, the blue-chip DAX index earlier ended the floor session at 3,028.67 points, up 51.96 points or 1.75 percent.

"It's the strong dollar that is underpinning everything today and no-one can afford to be out of the market," said one trader. "People are waiting for the plug to come out of the market. They are letting it go up now, but don't trust it in the long term."
German shares fell earlier on as the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street opened nearly one percent lower and the dollar fell below 1.64 marks, but recovered over the afternoon.
Recent favourite Deutsche Bank AG, the day's heaviest-traded stock, remained in favour and the bank gained 1.47 marks to 83.74 marks, albeit off earlier highs at 84.37.

Other star performers included car stocks, especially Daimler-Benz AG and Volkswagen AG. Daimler ended afternoon IBIS trade up one mark at 114.30 marks in afternoon IBIS trade, while Volkswagen advanced 27.50 marks to 769.50 marks.
"Daimler, Volkswagen are all having a great day and they are all dollar-driven. People are looking now to Siemens to outperform, because it's been an underperformer for so long," said the trader.

Siemens AG shares responded in kind and there was big turnover in the electronics giant. It was the second most-sought-after German stock in afternoon electronic trade, and ended the day up 63 pfennigs at 79 marks.

Dollar strength also lifted German chemical stocks -- BASF AG ended the day up 1.52 marks at 59.91 marks, Bayer AG ended up 95 pfennigs at 62.23 marks and Hoechst AG was up 97 pfennigs at 69.92 marks.

The biggest loser of the day was chemical and metals group Degussa AG, which finished electronic trade down 32.75 marks, or 4.40 percent, at 712.10, after an analysts' meeting disappointed analysts expectations for the group's outlook.
